entry.title: COP31: Johan Rockström Warns of Climate Tipping Points and Efforts to Sideline Science
entry.summary:
ANTALYA, Türkiye, November 17 (IPS) - The world is moving dangerously close to irreversible climate tipping points, making urgent action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions more critical than ever, warns Johan Rockström, Director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research. He argues that protecting forests and accelerating emissions reductions must go hand in hand to prevent further warming and preserve the planet’s natural capacity to absorb carbon dioxide.

Read the full story, “COP31: Johan Rockström Warns of Climate Tipping Points and Efforts to Sideline Science”, on globalissues.org →

entry.title: COP31: Four Nations Pledge $200 Million to GEF as Adaptation Costs Rise
entry.summary:
DAR ES SALAAM, Tanzania & ANTALYA, Türkiye, November 17 (IPS) - Four countries have pledged or proposed a combined $200 million for global environment and climate funds at the COP31 talks in Antalya, as developing nations press for more help to cope with droughts, floods and rising seas.

entry.title: Disparities in Birth and Death
entry.summary:
PORTLAND, USA, November 17 (IPS) - “Thou know’st ’tis common; all that lives must die, passing through nature to eternity.”(Hamlet) Although birth and death are universal human experiences, their timing and circumstances vary considerably within and across countries, contributing to significant differences in population growth rates. These differences also reflect profound disparities between privileged and marginalized populations.

entry.summary:
ANTALYA, Türkiye, November 17 (IPS) - Indigenous communities risk paying a heavy price for the global shift to clean energy unless governments involve them in decision-making and protect their ancestral territories, an Indigenous leader from Brazil has warned.

entry.title: Energy Transition only Works if Development Works
entry.summary:
BANGKOK, Thailand, November 17 (IPS) - The energy transition is reshaping economic structures across Asia and the Pacific. Where it is managed well, it can unlock new economic growth opportunities. Where it is not, it can trigger inflation and political backlash that stalls reform. The difference lies in whether transition policies are designed with socioeconomic development at their core.

entry.title: COP31: The push to protect warming oceans reaches the negotiating table
entry.summary:
From identifying marine life with a cup of seawater to drawing on Indigenous knowledge to prevent wildfires, scientists and communities showcased both cutting-edge and time-tested ways to protect nature at COP31 on Tuesday. Yet turning innovation into action remains a challenge, with funding gaps persisting and ministers struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance as negotiations enter their final days.
